doc.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Current playing: tuba, bass and Dixieland jobs
summary: He plays at least two nights a week, took up tuba during Broadway shows, and enjoys small Dixieland jobs.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well you seem to keep pretty busy with that and the work in the Local and you still go around this area playing bass.

Oh, yeah, I play at least two nights a week and sometimes more. I play a lot with Carmen Leggio over in Westchester, with Joe Shepley, he’s got a steady Wednesday down in Yonkers, I play with him, and all the guys come by to play with us so I get to play with George Young and Lou Delgado, guys like that, and some young players that Joe knows that are coming along real good. Well I took up the tuba while I was doing Broadway shows. I went back to a brass instrument after 25 years of not having touched one. And I found out I like the tuba a lot. So it relates very closely to a baritone horn, it’s just a larger member of the same family. So in order to keep my lip together on that I go rehearse with the Rockland County Concert Band and sometimes the Saddle River Concert Band down in New Jersey, and I do concerts with them when I can. And during the summer there’s a lot of Dixieland work on tuba, where my knowledge of those old tunes comes in handy. And once in a while, for economic reasons, they send out a group like to a store opening or an auto opening, where they want a kind of a Dixieland group but they don’t want to pay a full Dixieland band. So they’ll send out maybe drums, banjo, tuba and clarinet. Or one time I did it with just banjo and tuba. And I love those jobs because I get to fill in all of the missing parts. I can play the trombone parts, and I get to take a lot more solos that way you know, and it’s really interesting to me.
Wow. You must be tired by the time it’s done.

No it’s very refreshing. Once in a while if I haven’t been playing much during that week and then do a four hour job that’s a lot of playing, my lip will get tired, but it wakes me right up, makes me feel like playing music. It’s an interesting challenge.
